clue.text: Something to wear provided by job clubs, for example

parts.note: a job is one's business or line of work
clubs is one of the four suits in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Employment clubs hand out smart clothing to people looking for work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'job clubs' reads as one phrase about unemployment schemes, but 'job' and 'clubs' give separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A matching jacket and trousers for the office is a garment worn, so it is something put on.

clue.text: Inserting key undid a new building without help

indicators.note: inserting means putting a piece inside the rest
a new building is something put together afresh, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: E is a musical key

explanation.surface: Someone forces a key into a lock and dismantles a building on their own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new building' rearranges UNDID A into UNAIDD, and 'Inserting' puts E (a key in music) into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Unaided means done alone, with no assistance.

clue.text: Meandering circular

explanation.definitionFit: Indirect means roundabout, both wandering off course and taking a round route rather than a straight one.

clue.text: First person to enter before getting here

indicators.note: to enter means to go inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: ere is a poetic word for before
I is the first person pronoun

explanation.surface: Someone arrives ahead of others at a place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to enter' puts I inside ERE. 'here' defines the country only from the setter's own Irish viewpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the Irish name for Ireland, the place the speaker is in.

clue.text: Point to fool on board whip ping boys

indicators.note: on board means aboard a ship, so the pieces are put inside the ship's letters

parts.note: the ship boarded is SS, a steamship
a cape is a point of land jutting into the sea
a goat is slang for a fool, as in acting the goat

explanation.surface: Bullies on a ship pick on a weak boy to beat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' puts CAPE and GOAT inside SS, the abbreviation for steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Whipping boys are those blamed or punished for others' faults, as scapegoats are.

clue.text: Finished by getting higher

parts.note: up means over or finished, as in 'time's up'
per means by, as in 'per post'

explanation.surface: Ending up at a greater height.
explanation.definitionFit: Upper means further up, at a greater height.

clue.text: Swing leg up with ease, say

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a leg of a journey is a part of it

indicators.note: say means as if spoken, so the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: the word ease is said, giving its sound

explanation.surface: A gymnast lifts a leg effortlessly on a swing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns PART into TRAP; 'say' turns 'ease' into the sound EZE.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapeze is a bar on ropes that acrobats swing from, a circus swing.

clue.text: Some musicians could make them cry — not his!

indicators.note: could make means the letters could form something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A band could reduce listeners to tears, though not this one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make' rearranges THEM CRY and NOT HIS together, thirteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The drummer, bass player and similar players form the beat-keeping group of a band.

clue.text: An event I arranged, unable to see screen

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: unable to see means blind

explanation.surface: A blind person arranges an event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges AN EVENT I into VENETIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A slatted window shade is a screen keeping out light.

clue.text: Miser admitting nothing's more difficult?

indicators.note: admitting means letting something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: more difficult means harder
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A question about whether a stingy person's life is tougher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitting' puts O (nothing) inside HARDER; the question mark marks the playful surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser stockpiles money, and someone who stockpiles is a hoarder.

clue.text: Parrot swallowing seeds becomes calm

indicators.note: swallowing means taking something inside, so the seeds go into the parrot's word

parts.note: to parrot is to mimic, to ape
peas are the seeds of a pod plant

explanation.surface: A pet bird settles down after eating its seed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parrot' looks like the bird but works as the verb meaning mimic; the seeds sit inside after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To pacify someone is to make them calm, as appeasing an angry party does.

clue.text: Pointlessly toured rambling royal house

indicators.note: rambling means wandering about, so the remaining letters are rearranged
a point is a compass point, here E for east, so pointlessly means losing that letter

explanation.surface: Visitors wandered aimlessly round a palace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointlessly' removes E (east, a compass point) from TOURED, leaving TOURD; 'rambling' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudors were the English dynasty of Henry VIII and Elizabeth I, a ruling family.

clue.text: Relief, always through about one, returns

indicators.note: returns means comes back, so the whole assembled string is read backwards
about means surrounding, so the word for always goes round the one

parts.note: always means ever
one is the Roman numeral I
through means per, as in 'per post'

explanation.surface: A vague statement about relief recurring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns the whole string round, so the one sits near the start of the answer rather than the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprieve is a respite or temporary escape from trouble, a relief.

clue.text: Taking sister to Bali possibly improves passengers voyage

indicators.note: possibly means the letters might form something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A trip with a sister to Bali turns out better for everyone aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges SISTER and BALI; 'Taking' and 'to' are links. A ship's stabiliser fins cut rolling, making the voyage smoother.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's stabiliser reduces rolling, making a sea crossing more comfortable for those aboard.

clue.text: Drug doctor gets into a muddle

parts.note: a medic is a doctor

indicators.note: a muddle is a jumble, so the words before it are scrambled

explanation.surface: A doctor gets confused about which drug to prescribe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muddle' looks like part of the surface's confusion but is the anagram signal; 'gets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Medication is medicine given to a patient, a pharmaceutical.

clue.text: You once rejected it as something abominable!

parts.note: ye is an archaic word for you

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned exclamation that something is detestable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns IT into TI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalayan creature is popularly called the Abominable Snowman.

clue.text: Damned plant taken home by a man:

indicators.note: taken means taken in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: in means at home
Al is a man's name
a fern is a plant

explanation.surface: A man carries a plant into his house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' sets the home and the man side by side, and 'taken' then holds the plant between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Infernal means of hell, so belonging to the damned or accursed.

clue.text: Besides, Elsie's lost one

indicators.note: lost means no longer has, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: the name is taken as written, the 's meaning has
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: In addition, a woman has lost something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elsie's lost one' reads as Elsie has lost one: take I from ELSIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean in addition or otherwise, as in 'anything besides?'.

clue.text: Barred for dropping apple core, peeled

indicators.note: dropping means losing, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: peeled means stripped, as of its skin

indicators.note: the core of a fruit is its middle, so the central letter of the word is picked

explanation.surface: Someone was banned for throwing away an apple core after peeling it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'core' picks P, the middle letter of 'apple'; 'for dropping' removes one P from STRIPPED.
explanation.definitionFit: Barred describes something marked with bars or bands, which is what striped means.

clue.text: Not drinking alcohol sailor sent it on when at sea

parts.note: AB is an able seaman, a sailor

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sailor goes ashore and stays sober.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges SENT IT ON into STENTION; 'when' is a link. AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstention is refraining, here from drink, so it describes teetotal behaviour.

clue.text: Hill volunteers to consume unhealthy pancake

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor

indicators.note: to consume means to eat up, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
unhealthy means ill

explanation.surface: Hikers on a hill eat something bad for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'volunteers' is a common crossword signal for the TA, Britain's part-time reserve army.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortilla is a thin flat round of maize or wheat bread, a kind of flatbread like a thin pancake.

clue.text: Thoughts of the French as one's pushed in front

indicators.note: pushed in front means placed before the other pieces

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
de is French for of
taken as written

explanation.surface: An observation about French thinking in which someone pushes ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists the French word and 'as' first; 'pushed in front' moves the one ahead of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideas are notions formed in the mind, which is what thoughts are.

clue.text: She let poor man in

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece is put within the other
poor means badly made, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A woman allows a needy man into her home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges LET into ETL, and 'in' places the man inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a woman's first name, so it stands for a female, referred to as she.

clue.text: Asian with wet hair is hiding

indicators.note: is hiding says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone from Asia emerges with their hair dripping.
explanation.definitionFit: A Thai is a person from Thailand, a country of south-east Asia.

clue.text: Persecute work by journalists

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work
the press are journalists collectively

explanation.surface: A piece of writing by reporters.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppress is to treat harshly and unjustly, the same as hounding or persecuting.

clue.text: It's his job to make someone late

definitions.text: It's his job to make someone late

parts.words: It's his job to make someone late
parts.note: late here means dead, so the job is bringing about a death, by the rope

explanation.walkthrough: 'make someone late' sounds like delaying them, but 'late' means deceased.
explanation.definitionFit: An executioner by hanging makes condemned people 'the late' so-and-so, dead.

clue.text: Where Crusoe was to abandon lads in shipwreck?

parts.note: to desert is to abandon

indicators.note: a shipwreck breaks things apart, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A castaway story about men left behind after a wreck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shipwreck' rearranges LADS IN into ISLAND; 'to' is a link. Robinson Crusoe was shipwrecked on one in Defoe's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Defoe's Robinson Crusoe was marooned on an uninhabited isle.
